items.stem: Why is safety stock set from demand variability, not average demand alone?

options.text: Safety stock buffers against variability in demand and lead time, which the average hides
options.rationale: Correct: variability, not the mean, drives stockout risk.

options.text: Average demand already includes all variability
options.rationale: The average by definition removes variability.

options.text: Safety stock is unrelated to service level
options.rationale: Safety stock is set to hit a target service level.
Variability is the main driver of stockout risk.

items.explanation: Correct: variability, not the mean, drives stockout risk.

items.stem: Which TWO measures help dampen the bullwhip effect? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Share real downstream demand data across the chain
options.rationale: Correct: visibility reduces over-reaction to local signals.

options.text: Reduce order batching and smooth ordering
options.rationale: Correct: smaller, steadier orders cut amplification.

options.text: Have each stage guess demand independently in isolation
options.rationale: Isolation amplifies, not dampens, the bullwhip effect.

options.text: React to every short-term demand spike with a large reorder
options.rationale: Over-reaction is a primary cause of the bullwhip effect.

items.explanation: Correct: visibility reduces over-reaction to local signals.

items.stem: A forecast has low average absolute error but consistently under-predicts. What does this indicate?

options.text: A systematic forecast bias that should be corrected
options.rationale: Correct: consistent under-prediction is bias, distinct from error magnitude.
Persistent under-prediction means it is not unbiased.

options.text: Bias is irrelevant if MAPE is low
options.rationale: Bias matters independently of average error.
Correcting the bias is a clear improvement.
